scores.reason: It isolates a general mechanism, that the conservation list rather than the static symmetry selects the dynamic exponent, and tests it by holding statics fixed while varying conservation.
The claim is an exact identity, a log-ratio symmetry of the entropy-production distribution with slope exactly one, and the histogramming does not impose it.
A prospective quantitative claim that a one-unit change in order-parameter dimension shifts nu by more than declared magnitude and significance bars, with a null shift a reportable outcome.
It asserts an exact equality between two independently accumulated routes to the steady-state entropy production rate, plus a zero-drive control that the discretized dynamics could genuinely violate.
It tests a closed-form scaling identity linking eta to gamma/nu through two estimators built on disjoint moments of the ensemble, so agreement is a theorem rather than a construction.
It names an invariant, the extrapolated Binder cumulant as a shape observable of the class, and asserts its equality across component-matched pairs independently of any critical-coupling estimate.
It ties an integer structural quantity, the count of independent local conserved densities read off measured singular values, to the declared integrability-breaking strength along a frozen ladder.
A prospective quantitative claim of flux constancy and single-power-law spectrum over a pre-frozen band, with peak-to-peak, band-width, and endpoint-perturbation bars it can miss.

It identifies a structural transport signature, a finite ballistic weight tied to the presence of conserved structure and suppressed when that structure is broken, with a measured rather than imposed plateau.

It asserts that the linearized blocking map's largest eigenvalue is the mechanism fixing nu and that the result is invariant to the block factor, both testable in a truncated basis that need not deliver either.
A prospective quantitative claim about the size and monotonic growth in p of departures from the linear reference, with per-order significance and absolute bars and unconstrained fits.
A prospective magnitude claim that the fluctuation-dissipation ratio departs resolvably from its equilibrium value at declared two-time pairs, with an equilibrated control that can void the protocol.
It claims the conservation list is the component that sets the coarsening growth exponent, with a required inter-arm separation and separate power-law-form stability bars.
It posits a sharp dividing line in a continuously varying range parameter, requiring both a jump across the threshold and flatness within each side, neither of which is coded into the simulation.
It states a sufficiency claim for a named component list as the invariant fixing nu across microscopically different systems, with blinded labels and a required estimator-swap agreement first.
A well-posed registered null, predicting no ranking reversal between the two channels on this task pair, with the narrowed claim it would leave behind spelled out in advance.

It separates a channel-dependent quantity, the apparent slow-mode count, from a proposed channel-invariant one, the slowest relaxation rate, which is a structural decomposition that can come apart either way.

A prospective quantitative prediction of a rank correlation sign and a channel-pair swap with declared margins in zeta_6 and Brier score, where the threshold record is not defined in terms of the forecast event.
It asserts an invariance, that substrate exponents are representation-independent, alongside a claimed non-invariance of the consumer-relative spread, and stakes prior items on the outcome.

The task-asymmetry prediction with a declared saturation-ratio bar is a genuine prospective quantitative claim, but the collapse half follows from defining the top rung as the budget at which every channel is injective.

A prospective quantitative claim that coarse-graining and the exponent estimator fail to commute by a budget-dependent amount, with both vacuous and unsatisfiable outcomes declared in advance as failures.

It proposes a specific split, consumer-dependent prefactor and substrate-dependent exponent, in the approach of apparent entropy production to its microscopic value, and that split is exactly what the fit can break.

It distinguishes an ordering of experiments from a scalar ordering and predicts the observable signature of each, sign-consistent loss for nested channels and a task-dependent sign flip for incomparable ones.
A prospective quantitative prediction of both the order in which proposed survivors fail and the effective sample size at which the first failure occurs, bracketed to a declared factor-of-ten window.

A prospective quantitative claim that a named channel-task pair shows a non-monotone loss-versus-budget curve of declared size, with a realization-count test separating finite-sample from structural causes.
It names a specific structural source, the non-Gaussian tail of the local dissipation field, and tests it by two independent deletions that can kill the explanation while leaving the effect standing.
It identifies scale separation as the mechanism generating the cross-consumer exponent spread and predicts both a floor when it is deleted and a monotone regression on the separation ratio.
A prospective quantitative claim about the size and budget dependence of disagreement in a shared-band energy between two partially overlapping channels, with vacuous and void outcomes declared.

It commits to a specific survivor set across all admissible channels, including an entropy-production inequality and a correlation-length ordering, and names one non-survivor, so a larger or smaller set both count against it.
It commits to a directional split between what the channel moves, the exponents, and what it leaves invariant, the transition location, so getting the split backwards falsifies the decomposition.
